subject: Audit & retention: ephemeral-keystore parity and BYOK exception for NeuroSync POC
messages:
From: Alex Keller <alex.keller@neurosynclabs.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@neurosynclabs.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit & retention Qs for NeuroSync POC

Hi Mina —

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. We’re moving toward a short POC and our compliance team has a couple of asks before we can start ingesting any sensitive telemetry: 

- We need a clear retention matrix for logs and request traces (30/90/365 day options). Can Redwood provide a mapping for: request logs, KV cache dumps, and ephemeral keystore artifacts?
- BYOK: NeuroSync will need to hold the key material for the POC. We understand there’s a BYOK flow but our legal wants to confirm exception handling if we rotate/migrate keys during the pilot.
- SSO: we’ll use our IdP but we need assurance on session audit scoping (which events are forwarded to the audit export).

I attached our draft audit questions and the compliance intake form. If you can point us to a short owners matrix and expected timelines, we can clear internal signoffs.

Appreciate a quick sync — we’re targeting provisioning the POC environment next week.

—Alex
Alex Keller
Head of Platform Engineering
NeuroSync Labs
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Keller <alex.keller@neurosynclabs.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit & retention Qs for NeuroSync POC

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Priyom (infra/product interaction), Naomi (security/compliance), and Ben (audit ops) to triage. Below are quick responses and proposed next steps — I’ll follow up with a short call invite for Monday to lock owners and timeline.

Quick answers:
- Retention matrix: we can support configurable retention at three canonical tiers for the POC — 30d, 180d, and 3y — with per-artifact controls. For NeuroSync we recommend 30d for request-level traces, 180d for tokenized request logs, and 3y for billing/contractual audit exports. I’ve attached a starter matrix (neurosync-retention-matrix.xlsx) to this thread.
- BYOK exception: we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration. For short pilots we can offer a scoped exception that allows Redwood to rotate a delegated wrapping key if NeuroSync provides explicit rollback credentials and a migration plan. Naomi — can you confirm the list of conditions we require to approve a pilot exception?
- SSO/audit events: we will surface session start/stop, token issuance, and admin config changes by default. We can include more verbose request-body hashes on request if you need deeper forensic traces (this increases storage and cost).

Requested outcomes for Monday’s triage call:
1) Confirm NeuroSync’s selected retention tiers for each artifact type.
2) Decide whether the pilot will require a BYOK exception (and if so, complete the attached byok-exception-form.pdf).
3) Agree the scope of audit events to forward for the POC and whether we should enable request-body hashing.

I’ll send a calendar invite. Attachments: retention matrix + BYOK form + your audit questions.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Product & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Alex Keller <alex.keller@neurosynclabs.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit & retention Qs for NeuroSync POC

Thanks — added some technical notes from the infra side so NeuroSync has the perf/cost tradeoffs up front.

Technical constraints / proposals:
- Ephemeral keystore parity: we can maintain identical lifecycle semantics (create, rotate, retire) between hosted and private deployments, but we need a 48–72 hour lead to provision HSM-backed wrapping keys for BYOK pilots.
- Retention tiers: the smallest viable retention for request logs is 7 days in warm storage before cold-tier snapshotting; anything below 7d impacts debugging and request replay capability. If NeuroSync picks 30d we’re fine; for 30d we recommend weekly KV-cache snapshots to avoid warm-cache pressure.
- BYOK exception conditions (draft): signed exception form, explicit rollback credentials stored in NeuroSync vault, and a short-term key-escrow arrangement (30d) in case of emergency key loss. Naomi, please confirm the minimum audit evidence we need to record for the exception approval.

I’ve noted a couple of blockers for Canaries: if the POC requires request-body hashing for all requests, tokenization and batching optimizations will need to be disabled for the affected routes because hashing must precede aggregation — this will increase latency. Propose enabling hashing selectively on a small set of routes for the pilot.

Happy to discuss during the triage call — I can bring an infra runbook for the HSM provisioning path.

—Priyom
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Alex Keller <alex.keller@neurosynclabs.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit & retention Qs for NeuroSync POC

Alex / team —

Thanks for the patience while we reviewed the paperwork. Short summary of the approval conditions and next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

1) Retention plan approved (conditional): NeuroSync selects 30d for request traces, 180d for request logs, 3y for billing exports. We’ll add a clause that allows Redwood to escalate to 90d warm-window if debugging needs spike during the POC.

2) BYOK exception approved (pilot-limited): we need the completed byok-exception-form.pdf, NeuroSync’s rollback credentials (stored in their vault), and commitment to a 30d key-escrow holding period. Exception will be timeboxed to the POC term (45 days) and will include an audit checklist that Ben will maintain.

3) Audit events: default event set enabled. For request-body hashing we approve selective hashing on three named routes (please list them in the reply). If NeuroSync requests hashing across all traffic we’ll run an impact assessment first (Priyom to lead).

Action items / owners:
- NeuroSync: return signed BYOK form + list of three routes for selective hashing — Alex (owner).
- Priyom: HSM provisioning runbook and perf impact notes — due EOD Mon.
- Ben: create the audit checklist in Confluence and add a check-in cadence for the 45-day exception — Ben (owner).
- Mina: finalize the triage minutes and push final doc to the Confluence link below.

I’ve attached the finalized audit questions with the sections we need evidence for. Once Alex returns the signed BYOK form we can kick provisioning and schedule a short operational run with Priyom’s team.

—Naomi
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
